description: SB/BB facing a single open: defend by 3-bet (value+bluff) / call / fold. BB defends wide vs late opens; SB plays 3-bet-or-fold vs steals. v2 (N5): fills the 9 missing opener seats (BB vs UTG1/UTG2/LJ/HJ, SB vs UTG..HJ) by monotonic interpolation between the v1 anchors (RES-A method).

actions.combos: 22-99, A2s, A3s, A6s, A7s, A8s, A9s, ATs, AJs, K9s, KTs, KJs, KQs, Q9s, QTs, QJs, J9s, JTs, T8s, T9s, 98s, 87s, 76s, 65s, 54s, A9o, ATo, AJo, AQo, KTo, KJo, KQo, QJo, JTo

rationale_parts.lead: The button raised and you're in the big blind: defend very wide — folding too much here just hands over the blind you already paid.
points: You close the action and get roughly 30% pot odds (you call 1 to win about 3), so wide calls are cheap: flat the suited and connected hands, most pairs and offsuit Broadways.
3-bet (re-raise) TT+, AQs and AK for value.
A5s/A4s split 50/50 between 3-betting and calling — the wheel aces block AA/AK (holding an ace makes those less likely) and are strong enough to play either way.

actions.combos: 22-TT, ATs, AJs, A9s, KTs, KJs, KQs, QTs, QJs, JTs, T9s, 98s, 87s, 76s, 65s, AQo, KQo

rationale_parts.lead: The cutoff raised — a tighter range than a button raise — so defend your big blind one notch narrower.
points: 3-bet JJ+, AQs and AK for value, with A5s as the one bluff.
Still call wide (pairs, suited aces/Broadways, connectors down to 65s, AQo/KQo): your ~30% pot odds haven't changed, and over-folding the big blind gives up money you've already partly invested.
Only the very weakest connectors drop out compared to defending against the button.

actions.combos: 22-TT, ATs, AJs, A9s, KTs, KJs, KQs, QTs, QJs, JTs, T9s, 98s, 87s, 76s, AQo, KQo

rationale_parts.lead: The hijack raised — one seat earlier and slightly tighter than the cutoff — so shade your big-blind defense one hair inside the cutoff line.
points: Same value 3-bet: JJ+, AQs+, AK, with the A5s blocker bluff.
The calls keep the pairs and suited connectors but trim the bottom (65s drops).
AQo and KQo still defend — the hijack's range is wide enough that they aren't dominated too often.

actions.combos: 22-TT, AJs, ATs, A9s, KTs, KJs, KQs, QTs, QJs, JTs, T9s, 98s, 87s, AQo, KQo

rationale_parts.lead: The lojack raised: keep the same value 3-bet but downgrade the bluff, and trim the lowest connectors from your calls.
points: 3-bet JJ+, AQs+ and AK for value; A5s now splits 50/50 between 3-bet and call — an earlier-seat raiser calls your bluff with a stronger range more often.
Keep calling all pairs (set-mining odds still hold) and the suited-Broadway core.
76s/65s fold now: their implied odds (winning big when they hit) thin out against a tighter, stronger range.

actions.combos: 77-JJ, AQs, AJs, ATs, A9s, A5s, KTs, KJs, KQs, QJs, JTs, T9s, 98s

rationale_parts.lead: UTG+2's raise is still an early-position range, so 3-bet only the top and call with hands that flop well.
points: 3-bet only QQ+ and AK — light 3-bets burn money into a range this strong.
Call with 77–JJ (sets win big pots), the suited aces down to A9s/A5s, and suited Broadways plus KTs/98s that play well after the flop.

actions.combos: 99-JJ, AQs, AJs, ATs, A5s, KQs, KJs, QJs, JTs, T9s

rationale_parts.lead: One seat off UTG the raise is nearly as strong, so defend nearly as tight as against UTG itself.
points: 3-bet only QQ+ and AK.
Call a tight, high-quality band: 99–JJ, AQs–ATs, suited Broadways, JTs, plus A5s and T9s for playability.

actions.combos: 99-JJ, AQs, AJs, ATs, KQs, KJs, QJs, JTs, TT

rationale_parts.lead: UTG's raise is the strongest range at the table: 3-bet only premiums and call with a tight band of hands that flop well.
points: 3-bet QQ+ and AK for value only — bluffing into this range gets punished.
Call with 99–JJ, AQs–ATs, suited Broadways and JTs: strong enough to continue when the flop cooperates.
Small pairs and suited gappers fold — their big-payoff potential collapses against a range this strong.

actions.combos: 55+, A8s+, KTs+, QTs+, J9s+, T9s, AJo+, KQo, A5s, A4s

rationale_parts.lead: The button raised and you're in the small blind: it's 3-bet or fold — calling just signs you up to play the whole hand out of position with a capped hand.
points: 3-bet a merged range (strong hands plus good-but-not-premium ones): 55+, suited aces from A8s, suited Broadways, J9s+/T9s, AJo+/KQo, and A5s/A4s as blockers.
That's wide enough to punish a button steal, strong enough to play a raised pot out of position.
Everything else folds rather than calling into a positional disadvantage.

rationale_parts.lead: Same 3-bet-or-fold rule against a cutoff raise, tightened one notch because the cutoff opens stronger than the button.
points: 3-bet 77+, ATs+, KJs+, QJs, AQo+ with A5s as the lone bluff.
The range stays merged (value plus strong playable hands, not just premiums-and-bluffs) — you never want to flat out of position against a range that already beats yours.

rationale_parts.lead: Against a hijack raise, tighten the small-blind 3-bet another notch — and still never just call.
points: 3-bet 88+, ATs+, KQs, AQo+ with the A5s blocker bluff.
The suited-Broadway tail (KJs/QJs) drops out — the earlier raiser's range dominates it too often.

rationale_parts.lead: Against a lojack raise the small blind tightens again: 3-bet a strong merged core or fold.
points: 3-bet 99+, AJs+, KQs, AQo+ with the A5s blocker.
Mid pairs and dominated suited aces shift from profitable 3-bets to folds — the opening range is simply too strong now.

actions.combos: TT+, AJs+, KQs, AKo, AQo, A5s

rationale_parts.lead: An early-position raise pushes the small blind toward premiums: 3-bet the top or fold.
points: 3-bet TT+, AJs+, KQs, AQo+ with A5s as the only bluff.
Anything weaker is either an outright fold or gets dominated too often to 3-bet into an early-position range.

rationale_parts.lead: One seat off UTG, the small-blind defense narrows to near-premiums only.
points: 3-bet TT+, AQs+, AKo plus the A5s blocker.
AJs and AQo become folds — UTG+1's range dominates them too frequently to re-raise out of position.

rationale_parts.lead: The table's strongest range raised and you're in the worst seat: premiums or fold — nearly everything folds here, and that's correct.
points: 3-bet only QQ+, AQs+, AKo plus the single A5s blocker — about 2.6% of hands.
The thinness is the honest answer, not a gap in the chart: against UTG from the small blind, folding is usually the money-saving play.
